caption:
Canada's stock market just had one of its worst days of the year — and it hit RRSPs and TFSAs directly.

The S&P/TSX composite fell about 737 points Wednesday, roughly 2%, its third straight drop (Canadian Press, Nov. 18). Gold and oil both tumbled, and because the index is stacked with miners, energy and banks, the big dividend stocks most Canadians hold all fell at once.

One upside: January crude slid to about US$82 a barrel — cheaper oil points to lower gas down the road.

My take: a resource-heavy index cuts both ways. It sinks your RRSP on a day like this, but cheaper oil quietly helps at the pump.
